---
title: "Preface"
---

A coding agent is a collaborator with no memory and no stake in being right. It writes
plausible code quickly, and plausible is not the same as correct. So the useful question
is not *can it fit the model* — it is **what can I delegate, and how do I check it?**

This is the written version of a workshop given at the University of New Mexico. It is a
walkthrough, not an assignment: everything in it runs on one public repository and one
real research question — did Latino voters in the Western states shift toward Trump
between 2020 and 2024, and does authoritarianism condition that shift?

## Goals

1. See the whole loop once — **clone, branch, diff, undo** — on a real project.
2. See how an agent comes to **know a project** through an instruction file.
3. Watch one substantive question get answered, and watch us **check the machine's work**.

## How this is organized

**Before you start** — [Downloads](00-resources.qmd): what to install, how to check
it worked, and the zero-install paths if you would rather not install anything.

**The workflow** — [Framing](01-framing.qmd) on what an agent is and where it fails
silently; [Setup](02-setup.qmd); the [git workflow](03-git.qmd) that makes delegation
safe; and [Agents](04-agents.qmd), on instruction files and the commands worth knowing.

**The pipeline** — the [overview](05-pipeline.qmd), then one chapter per stage:
[the data](06-data.qmd), [the recode](07-recode.qmd), [the analysis](08-analysis.qmd),
[the tests](09-tests.qmd), and [the app and publishing](10-app-and-publishing.qmd).
These chapters run the repository's own scripts, so the numbers and figures in them are
the ones the code actually produces.

**Checking the work** — [Verification](11-verification.qmd): reading the diff, citing
the codebook, reporting *n*, and turning a check into a test.

## Running the code

The repository is public, so read access is all you need:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop.git
cd UNM_Workshop
Rscript R/01_recode.R
Rscript R/02_analysis.R
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
quarto render                 # rebuild this book
```

::: {.note}
[About the code chunks]{.note-head}
Chapters with output execute against `data/wss_2020_2024.csv`, which is in the
repository. Results are cached with Quarto's `freeze`, so rebuilding the book does not
re-run everything — but deleting `_freeze/` and rendering again is the real test of
reproducibility.
:::

::: {.warn}
[About the data]{.warn-head}
The Western States Survey file here is pared down for teaching. Variable meanings come
from the codebooks in `codebooks/` — cite those, not this book, and not the agent.
:::
